headline: Hidden Conditions in Older Kitchens
articleBody: Older kitchens in Los Angeles County often reveal hidden conditions once walls and floors are opened. Common issues include outdated electrical panels or undersized branch circuits, ungrounded receptacles, old galvanized or corroded plumbing, nonstandard framing, prior unpermitted modifications, and water damage around sinks, windows, or slab penetrations. Local building and safety agencies regularly note that hidden conditions are a normal risk in remodeling because kitchens combine water, power, and structural modifications in a compact space. In many older homes, the electrical system may not support the demand of modern appliances, which can require new circuits, GFCI and AFCI protections depending on the installation, and sometimes panel upgrades. Plumbing relocations can also reveal patchwork repairs or incompatible materials from prior work. From a contracting perspective, these unknowns matter because they affect both cost and schedule; a contractor who has remodeled older homes in the region should be prepared to document conditions quickly and propose code-compliant corrections. Homeowners should ask how the contractor handles concealed discoveries, whether an allowance or contingency is built into the budget, and who approves repairs before extra work begins. A remodel plan that assumes hidden-condition surprises is usually more realistic than one that treats the existing structure as ideal.
